senses.definition: A state of tranquility, quiet, and harmony. For instance, a state free from civil disturbance.
examples: Our lounge strives to maintain an environment of peace for the comfort of our customers.

quotes.text: *Thinke not that I am come to ſend peace on earth: I came not to ſend peace, but a ſword.
quotes.reference: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London: […] Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Matthew 10:34:

quotes.text: Naomi boasted in nothing but the God of Israel. And she found peace even in the midst of chaos when she went to Him in prayer.

senses.definition: A feeling of tranquility, free from oppressive and unpleasant thoughts and emotions.
examples: The safety equipment will give me some peace of mind.

quotes.text:
’Twere best at once to sink to peace,
⁠Like birds the charming serpent draws,
⁠To drop head-foremost in the jaws
Of vacant darkness and to cease.

senses.definition: A state free of war, in particular war between different countries.
examples:

quotes.text: An uneasy peace descended upon Northern Ireland when the IRA agreed to a ceasefire in August 1994.

senses.definition: (archaic) Shut up!, silence!; be quiet, be silent.

quotes.text:
“Hark!” said the old woman, triumphantly. “I hear a step coming. […] Do you hear him?”
“I believe you are right, mother,” replied Alice, in a low voice. “Peace! open the door.”
